one_liner: Copy of the two-header NanoSVG parser and rasterizer with SSE2 blending and span-delta coverage, 2.5-3.7x faster than its own previous rasterizer.
what_it_does: Parses SVG files into lists of cubic Bezier paths (nanosvg.h) and rasterizes them into a caller-provided RGBA8 buffer with a small scanline rasterizer (nanosvgrast.h). The API is NanoSVG's: nsvgParseFromFile/nsvgParse, then nsvgCreateRasterizer and nsvgRasterize(rast, image, tx, ty, scale, dst, w, h, stride), so code written against upstream memononen/nanosvg compiles unchanged. It handles solid fills, linear and radial gradients and strokes with joins, caps and dashes; there is no clipping, masking, filters, text or embedded images.
how_it_is_fast: The rasterizer is NanoSVG's 5-subsample scanline converter with exact horizontal fixed-point coverage; the fork stores fully covered spans as start/end deltas in an int array and prefix-sums them once per pixel row instead of adding 51 to every byte five times per row. The blend loop fuses that prefix sum with SSE2 4-pixel source-over blending (div255 as _mm_mulhi_epu16(x+1, 257)), skips zero-coverage pixels, writes fully opaque runs directly, evaluates gradient colors only for covered pixels, starts at the first edge's row and stops when edges run out, and limits the unpremultiply/defringe pass to the drawn bounding box using 24-bit reciprocals instead of divisions. It also stops zero-length cubics from recursing 2047 times in the flattener, and the parser replaces strtoll/pow/sscanf/strchr with hand-written digit loops and power-of-ten tables.
when_to_use: Baking SVG icons or UI glyphs into textures at load time in a game or tool, where a two-header, dependency-free C library is worth more than full SVG conformance.
You already ship upstream NanoSVG and want a faster drop-in rasterizer on x86-64 without changing call sites.
Small to medium images (tens to a few hundred pixels per side) with simple fills and gradients, rendered on one thread per rasterizer object.
Builds that cannot pull in C++ or a large dependency tree (Cairo, Skia, Blend2D).
when_not_to_use: You need correct rendering of real-world SVG: no clip paths, masks, filters, patterns, text, <use> handling beyond the parser's support, or embedded images; the inherited README still calls the rasterizer 'not particular fast or accurate'.
Quality matters: anti-aliasing uses only 5 vertical subsamples per pixel, so near-horizontal edges show visible banding compared with analytic-coverage renderers.
Non-x86 targets expect the full gain: the SSE2 path is x86 only, and PR #3's own NSVG_NO_SIMD column runs about 1.0-1.1x the post-PR #2 code, so ARM gets roughly the PR #2 algorithmic speedup only.
You need upstream NanoSVG's newer features: this copy lacks upstream's paint-order support (shape->paintOrder) and uses its own 2024 CSS style handling rather than upstream's class-based one.
You want a maintained, reviewed library: 0 stars, 12 commits, all speed work landed on 2026-09-24 from an AI-agent branch, and no tests or fuzzing harness are in the repo.

integration.dependencies: none beyond libc and libm (stdio.h, string.h, stdlib.h, math.h); emmintrin.h for the SSE2 path
integration.min_toolchain: C99 for nanosvg.h (the CDATA skip in nsvg__parseXML declares a variable after a statement); nanosvgrast.h is stated to build with -std=c89 -pedantic; CMake 3.10 for the optional package
integration.platforms: any; SSE2 fast path on x86-64 (GCC, Clang, MSVC) and 32-bit MSVC with /arch:SSE2, scalar elsewhere or with NSVG_NO_SIMD
integration.thread_safety: not documented; no mutable globals in either header, but an NSVGrasterizer holds scratch buffers, so use one rasterizer per thread

gotchas: Output is not byte-identical to the pre-PR code or to upstream: PR #2 fixes the defringe check (x-1 > 0 became x > 0), which changes the color of fully transparent pixels in column 1 and row 1, and the hex color parser now rejects malformed colors (spaces, signs, 0x prefixes) that the sscanf version accepted.

nsvgRasterize still clears the whole destination buffer each call, so it cannot composite onto existing pixels; the unpremultiply pass then runs only over the drawn bounding box plus a one-pixel border.
Coverage still wraps modulo 256 like the original unsigned char sums, so heavily overlapping sub-paths under the nonzero rule keep NanoSVG's existing artifacts.

The repository is a standalone copy of a 2024 NanoSVG snapshot with local parser changes (title capture, CDATA skipping, rgba alpha), not a GitHub fork, so upstream fixes do not flow in automatically.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over LunaSVG or ThorVG when you want two C headers with no build step and only need flat fills, gradients and strokes for icon baking; pick LunaSVG for a C++ renderer with much broader SVG support, and Blend2D or ThorVG when rendering quality, clipping or throughput on large scenes matter.
verified_claims_summary: The fork's own PRs time its rasterizer against its pre-PR master (essentially upstream NanoSVG's 2024 rasterizer) on example/23.svg, drawing.svg, nano.svg and a gradient test at 1x and 3x scale, -O2 on x86-64 with no CPU or compiler version: PR #2 reports 2.5-3.7x (mean of 40 runs) and PR #3 adds 1.34-1.98x with SSE2 (best of 11, callgrind counts); no harness is committed, and the two PRs' absolute times are not comparable, so the gains should not be multiplied. Reading the diffs found no correctness bug behind these numbers: the SSE2 blend, coverage prefix sum and reciprocal unpremultiply match the scalar arithmetic (the reciprocal identity holds for all 8-bit inputs when rechecked).
status_note: Active only in the sense that the owner merged three AI-authored PRs on 2026-09-24 (0 stars, README still says 'not actively maintained'); zlib-licensed and two headers, so it is easy to vendor, but treat it as a lightly tested patch set over NanoSVG.
